guidance.title: What the GitLab token needs
guidance.token: Create a project access token in this project only (in the project's settings, under Access tokens): role Developer, scopes api, read_repository and write_repository. Never Maintainer or Owner, and never a group or personal token.
guidance.expiry: GitLab tokens expire, at most a year after they are made. Make the next token before this one expires and save it on the connection: the page warns you 30 days ahead.
guidance.branch: Protect the default branch (no force push, push and merge for Maintainers only), require pipelines to succeed before a merge, and leave voc-agent/* branches unprotected.

points.protected_secrets: CI/CD variables that hold secrets are protected, so only pipelines on protected branches get them.
points.read_only_token: The CI/CD job token has the least access: its allowlist holds only the projects the pipelines need, and no job pushes with it.
points.oidc_pinned: Cloud access through OIDC (id_tokens) is pinned to protected branches (the token’s ref_protected claim).
points.no_self_hosted_runner: No shared, group or instance runner with access to secrets or private networks runs jobs for unprotected branches: such runners are protected.
points.no_privileged_pull_request: No pipeline runs merge request code with secrets: no merge request pipeline for forks in this project, and no protected variable reaches one.
points.branch_rules: The default branch is protected (no force push, push and merge for Maintainers), pipelines must succeed before a merge (a skipped pipeline does not count as a success), the CI configuration uses only plain local includes and GitLab's own templates (shared CI from other projects, remote includes and components are not supported), and voc-agent/* branches stay unprotected.

ci.checked: The broker also reads the protected branches at each push and merge request: the default branch protected with no force push and push and merge for Maintainers, pipelines required to succeed, and voc-agent/* branches not protected.

connections.notSetHint: The stored credential is missing: edit the connection and save it with its credential again.

guidance.title: What the credential needs
guidance.app: Create a GitHub App and install it only on this repository. Repository permissions: Contents, Pull requests and Issues set to Read and write, Metadata to Read-only. Nothing else: no Administration, Workflows, Secrets, Actions or organization permission.
guidance.token: The App is never handed to the agents: for each step the broker mints a token valid for one hour, for this one repository and only what the step needs of the App's permissions (Contents, Pull requests and Issues, read and write; Metadata, read-only; never admin).
guidance.branch: Protect the default branch, and let the agents push only to branches named voc-agent/*.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisites
prerequisites.summary: What every automation stands on: the repository connected through the deployment's GitHub App, its CI attested, and its issues ingested for the whole deployment.
prerequisites.skipCost: Without them no automation can run: a run needs the repository connected through the App and its CI attested, and the issue automations need its issues ingested. Enable stays off until the checks a run needs pass.

understand.title: Understand the repository
understand.summary: A pass over the repository that writes down what the agents should know of it: its packages, how each builds and tests, and where things live. Its pull request is a person's to review.
understand.skipCost: Without it the agents learn the repository from scratch on every run: findings are shallower, a fix touches the wrong place more often, and runs take longer and cost more.

tenets.title: Tenets
tenets.summary: The project's tenets, written down and accepted by an administrator: what triage and reviews judge an issue and a change by.
tenets.skipCost: Without tenets, triage has no stated priorities to judge an issue by, and reviews judge a change by the code alone: severities are less consistent, and a fix can go against what the project values.

triage.title: Issue triage
triage.summary: Reads each labelled issue, classifies it as a bug, a feature or an investigation, rates its severity, writes its acceptance criteria, then comments and labels the issue. Bug fixer and Feature builder start from its triage.
triage.skipCost: Without triage, Bug fixer and Feature builder decide from the issue's own label and words: a feature request can reach the bug fixer, severity is guessed, and a fix starts without acceptance criteria.

bug_fixer.title: Bug fixer
bug_fixer.summary: Hunts the bug an issue reports, fixes it with a test that fails without the fix, runs the repository's quality gate, then pushes and opens the pull request that says Fixes #N. A person approves and merges it on GitHub.
bug_fixer.skipCost: Without it, labelled bugs are triaged, but nothing fixes them or opens a pull request.

feature_builder.title: Feature builder
feature_builder.summary: Builds what a feature issue or a project's PRD asks for, through the same quality gate, then opens its pull request for a person to review and merge.
feature_builder.skipCost: Without it, feature requests are triaged, but nothing builds them, and a PRD's Build from this PRD has no agent to hand it to.
